Up here, in pretty much all of Canada we let the big ones go and the small ones grow and take eaters from in the middle, because the big ones have the good genetics and lay the most and best eggs, Also spring is the spawning season for most fish so it matters now more then any other time of year.

Also smaller fish taste better, the meat is firmer and cleaner tasting, with pike you don't want to keep them too small either because they have an extra set of bones called Y bones(because they are shaped like a Y), and after you clean them there's not as much meat as you'd think. I like to keep pike about 26"-36" so like 5-15lbs.

Also with all the pictures and social media not as many people are into keeping the trophy sized fish for taxedermy trophy mounts anymore. take a picture take a measurement and let it go. Also with pictures and measurements you can get an artificial mount if you really want one for cheaper and that's honstely better quality. So let the trophy fish breed more trophy fish.
